messages.content: New work trip: Denver Water Technology Conference. Dates are Tue Jun 23-Thu Jun 25. Booth setup Tuesday afternoon, customer meetings Wednesday, breakouts Thursday. The official block is Hyatt Regency at the convention center, $239. Someone suggested The Maven by Dairy Block, about $289. Need a flight/hotel shortlist from SFO or OAK, practical nonstops only unless there’s a shockingly better reason. Monday afternoon arrival is okay; Tuesday morning only if it lands before noon. Return Thursday is fuzzy because teardown may keep me late.

I’ll compare this as two arrival patterns: arrive Mon Jun 22 with prep time, or Tue Jun 23 with lower hotel cost. For Thursday, I’ll separate a clean early-evening return from a late hedge so you are not forced into a Friday unless teardown really slips.
Good. No SJC unless it is dramatically cleaner. I don’t want to save $70 and add a messy airport day.

Outbound shortlist: 1) Mon United SFO-DEN 1:35-5:10, usually around $210-$240 one way; calmest. 2) Mon Southwest OAK-DEN 2:15-5:45, similar fare, easier checked bag math, but OAK adds commute. 3) Tue United SFO-DEN 8:05-11:40, cheaper by about $60-$90; workable only if booth setup can tolerate a delay. 4) Tue Southwest OAK-DEN 6:40-10:05, cheapest but early and less forgiving.
Booth setup is listed 1:00-5:00, but I’ll have the membrane demo case and badges to deal with. Tuesday landing before noon sounds thin.

Agreed. If the case matters, Monday is the best fit. A Tuesday 11:40 arrival puts you at the convention center roughly 12:35-12:50 if baggage and rideshare behave. Any delay eats the setup window. Tuesday is an acceptable backup only if someone else can start the booth.
Hotel tradeoff next. Is the Hyatt block a safe choice, or just convenient?

Hyatt Regency Convention Center: best for convenience. It is effectively across or attached to the convention center, around $239, guest ratings around 4.3, on-site restaurant/bar, and easy badge logistics. Downsides: busy lobby, conference crowd, and less interesting dinner radius. The Maven: stronger guest feedback, about 4.6, near Dairy Block and Union Station restaurants, likely quieter if you request an interior room, but about $50 more per night and a 5-10 minute rideshare or 15-minute walk to sessions.
Wednesday dinner may land downtown, not sure where. I want easy restaurants but not a boutique-hotel tax just for fun.

If dinner ends up near Union Station or LoDo, The Maven saves time and friction. If most days are convention-center-heavy, Hyatt is the practical pick and still clears the quality bar. The cost gap is roughly $150 before tax for a Monday-Thursday stay, plus any rideshares.
Do those rooms have a coffee maker and mini-fridge? Three conference mornings without both is annoying.

Hyatt standard rooms list a coffee maker and mini-fridge. The Maven lists an in-room fridge and coffee setup, though I’d put both in the booking notes and confirm before finalizing. Neither is a reason to reject them, but I would verify The Maven’s room category.
Return options?

Thursday DEN to Bay Area: early option United DEN-SFO about 6:15-7:55, good if you can leave the hall by 4:15. Middle option Southwest DEN-OAK around 7:30-9:05, useful if OAK is okay and baggage timing is uncertain. Late hedge United DEN-SFO around 8:45-10:25, least stressful if teardown runs to 5:30.
I’d rather not stay until Friday unless freight goes sideways. Is booking a later Thursday return and moving earlier dumb?

Not dumb. The late United return is the safer placeholder for SFO; you can move earlier if teardown gets covered, subject to fare difference. Southwest is easier to cancel to credit, but it sends you to OAK. If the company wants clean receipts, one-way outbound plus hotel now and return after freight is also clean.
Give me the shortlist you’d send to my manager.

Best fit: Mon Jun 22 United SFO-DEN 1:35-5:10, Hyatt block if budget/convention access is the priority, The Maven if Wednesday dinner and quieter evenings matter more, and a late Thursday SFO return as the hedge. Acceptable backup: Tue Jun 23 United SFO-DEN 8:05-11:40 only if a teammate can receive materials or start booth setup. I would avoid the early OAK option unless price becomes the deciding factor.
For now assume I’m personally responsible for setup. Put The Maven and Hyatt side by side, no booking yet.

Side by side: Hyatt is lower cost and lowest logistics risk for the booth; The Maven is higher rated, better for dinners, and a better sleep bet if you get a quiet room. With you owning setup, I’d lean Monday arrival either way. Ask before booking: confirm whether the extra $150-ish for The Maven is acceptable and whether to hold the late Thursday return or leave the return open until teardown is assigned.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Denver was narrowed after booth access moved earlier: Monday afternoon SFO-DEN and The Maven were selected, while the return remains pending the Thursday freight handoff.

messages.content: Update on Denver: booth access moved to 11:30 Tuesday, and the manufacturer dinner is confirmed near Union Station Wednesday. Teammate may handle final freight Thursday, but not confirmed. Narrow this.

That makes the Tuesday-morning flight much less attractive. If you land at 11:40, you are already behind the new access window and would hit the hall around 12:40 with no disruption margin. Best fit is now Monday afternoon SFO-DEN. Hotel lean also moves toward The Maven because Wednesday dinner is near Union Station.
Is Monday afternoon overkill? I’m trying not to add cost just because it’s nicer.

The extra night is the cost, but it buys the setup buffer. With 11:30 access, Tuesday only works if delays are minor and someone else can handle badge/materials. For a demo case and customer meetings, Monday is schedule insurance, not comfort padding.
Okay, Monday. Which hotel would you actually pick?

The Maven is the best fit now: stronger guest feedback, easiest Wednesday dinner logistics, and a quieter-room request is realistic. Hyatt block is the acceptable backup if the manager pushes back on rate or wants you steps from the booth.
What’s the actual delta for Monday through Thursday?

Hyatt: about $239 x 3 before tax. Maven: about $289 x 3 before tax. So roughly $150 pre-tax extra. You may save one or two rideshares around dinner, but not enough to erase it. The real benefit is the better evening location and room feedback.
Make sure the room request is quiet, not over a bar. And confirm fridge/coffee.
I’d book The Maven refundable king or queen, request high floor/interior or courtyard-facing, away from elevator and bar noise, and add a note to confirm mini-fridge plus in-room coffee setup.
Return: if teammate covers freight, I can take the 6:15. If not, 8:45. I don’t know until tomorrow.

Then don’t lock the return yet unless fares jump. Keep the outbound and hotel moving today; tomorrow choose 6:15 if freight handoff is done by 4:15, otherwise 8:45. Both keep you out of a Friday stay.
Book the Monday SFO outbound and The Maven refundable. Hold off on return. Window seat if there’s one.
Before I book: United SFO-DEN Mon Jun 22, 1:35-5:10, economy; The Maven Jun 22-25, refundable standard room with quiet-room, fridge, and coffee notes; no return yet. Correct?
Correct. Use SFO and the refundable rate.

Booked: United SFO-DEN Mon Jun 22 1:35 p.m.-5:10 p.m., seat 21A window. The Maven is reserved Jun 22-25 on the refundable rate with quiet-room, mini-fridge, and coffee notes. Return remains open: target 6:15 p.m. DEN-SFO if the teammate takes freight, otherwise 8:45 p.m. DEN-SFO. Follow up tomorrow once freight is confirmed.
